name: Copenhagen Plank
description: The Copenhagen plank is an advanced side plank variation in which the top leg is supported on a bench or box while the bottom leg hangs or is adducted upward. It is one of the most effective exercises for training the hip adductors under a high-force isometric demand while simultaneously loading the lateral core. Research has demonstrated its effectiveness in both adductor strengthening and groin injury prevention in sports athletes.

execution.starting_position: Position a flat bench alongside you. Rest the top ankle or shin on the bench edge in a side plank position with the forearm on the floor. The bottom leg hangs beneath the bench.
execution.setup_instructions: Set a bench at a height that challenges the adductors — typically 40–50 cm. The top leg should be supported at the ankle for maximum leverage.
steps: Step 1: Set up with the top ankle or shin on the bench, bottom forearm on the floor, and body in a straight side-plank line.
Step 2: Drive the top leg down into the bench and simultaneously lift the hips off the floor to form a straight plank line.
Step 3: The bottom leg can either hang (supported hold) or be lifted to meet the top leg (dynamic version).
Step 4: Hold the position with hips fully extended and body in a straight line.
Step 5: Lower with control. Perform equal sets on each side.
execution.breathing_instructions: Breathe shallowly and continuously during the hold.
common_mistakes: Allowing the hips to drop, reducing adductor tension
Rotating the torso forward or backward
Using the ankle — placing the foot on the bench instead of the ankle/shin reduces adductor leverage
safety_considerations: Groin soreness in the days following initial training is normal — progress load conservatively.
If experiencing groin pain, regress to a short-lever Copenhagen plank with the knee on the bench.
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full isometric hold with hips elevated and body straight. Progress from short-lever (knee on bench) to long-lever (ankle on bench).
execution.tempo_recommendations: Hold for 10–30 seconds. Progress duration before adding dynamic repetitions.
coaching_cues: Drive the top leg into the bench
Keep your hips tall — no sagging
Straight line from shoulder to ankle
